title: Retrospective Analysis of Metabolic Data from Intensive Care Medicine
summary:
Adequate energy supply is important for critically ill patients in intensive care. Both insufficient and excessive energy supply may be associated with complications.

Energy requirements can be estimated using calculation formulas or determined using a specific measurement method. This method measures energy expenditure based on oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production.

The aim of this study is to investigate differences between men and women regarding measured and calculated energy requirements. In addition, the study examines whether the amount of energy actually provided corresponds to the determined energy requirements.

For this purpose, existing treatment data from patients admitted to the surgical intensive care unit at Cologne-Merheim Hospital will be analyzed retrospectively.
conditions: Energy requirements and clinical nutritional therapy in critically ill patients in the surgical intensive care unit.

interventions.name: Retrospective observational study analyzing energy requirements and clinical nutritional therapy in adult patients admitted to a surgical intensive care unit. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients treated in the surgical intensive care unit at Klinikum Merheim
Age ≥ 18 years
Invasive mechanical ventilation via intubation or tracheotomy
Indirect calorimetry performed
Existing indication for artificial nutrition
Exclusion criteria:
FiO₂ > 80%
PEEP > 8 mbar
Core body temperature > 38°C
Hyperchloremia
Body mass index > 40 kg/m²
Hypernatremia (serum sodium > 150 mmol/L)
